messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius.

We need to use the tool `requests_get` to fetch data from Open-Meteo API. We have to provide appropriate query params: latitude & longitude for White Plains. Let's find approximate coordinates: White Plains, NY ~ lat 41.0535°N, lon -73.7629°W. So latitude=41.0535, longitude=-73.7629.

Open-Meteo API supports daily forecasts including temperature_2m_max/min etc. For next week we can get daily max/min temps. Use "daily": ["temperature_2m_min", "temperature_2m_max"], maybe also precipitation probability. Provide timezone param as local tz e.g., America/New_York.

Also specify start_date and end_date: today +1 day? Next week meaning upcoming seven days starting tomorrow? Or next calendar week? We'll assume next 7 days from current date inclusive. But easier: set start_date=today+1, end_date=today+7. Need to compute dates programmatically but can't run code here. Could just ask for next week's forecast using open-meteo's /forecast? Actually open-meteo has endpoint `/v1/forecast`. Example:

https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&hourly=temperature_2m&start=YYYY-MM-DDT00:00Z&end=YYYY-MM-DDT23:59Z

But simpler: daily forecast: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=41.0535&longitude=-73.7629&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min&timezone=Africa/Cairo? No, timezone=America/New_York.

We'll call the function accordingly.

Let's craft JSON payload:

{
"url": "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
"params":{
   "latitude": 41.0535,
   "longitude": -73.7629,
   "daily":["temperature_2m_max","temperature_2m_min"],
   "timezone":"America/New_York"
}
}

However the schema expects each param individually not array? In the definition, params includes fields like latitude, longitude, elevation only. It doesn't support arrays directly. Might need to pass them via query string manually. But our tool may accept arbitrary keys inside params dict. It's okay.

Alternatively we could construct full URL ourselves: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=41.0535&longitude=-73.7629&daily=temperature_2m_max%2Ctemperature_2m_min&timezone=America%2FNew_York"

Better to supply url fully encoded.

Thus we'll do:

{
"url":"https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=41.0535&longitude=-73.7629&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min&timezone=America/New_York"
}

No headers needed.

Return result.

Then parse output into readable summary.

Ok let's proceed.
